---
title: Blueprint anatomy
description: "The files that make up a template and the rules every blueprint follows."
---

**Purpose** — A blueprint is one folder under `templates/blueprints/` in the Notploy repository, mirrored at `/blueprints/<id>/` on every gallery host. This page describes its files, the metadata contract and the Compose rules the validators enforce.

## Files

| File | Required | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docker-compose.yml` | Yes | The stack Notploy deploys. |
| `template.toml` | Yes | Variables, environment, domains and file mounts generated on import. |
| `meta.json` | Yes | Catalogue metadata: identity, links and tags. |
| `<logo>.svg` (or `.png`, `.webp`, `.jpg`) | Yes | Logo referenced by the `logo` field of `meta.json`. |
| `instructions.md` | No | Setup guide rendered in the gallery's *Instructions* tab. |
| `README.md` | No | Notes for people reading the repository. |

A blueprint is valid only when `docker-compose.yml`, `template.toml` and `meta.json` are all present — that is also what the panel checks when it lists blueprints from a local checkout.

## meta.json

Every blueprint owns its metadata in its own folder, so pull requests never touch a shared file and merge conflicts cannot happen. The build aggregates the per-folder files into the single catalogue the gallery serves at `/meta.json`.

```json
{
  "id": "grafana",
  "name": "Grafana",
  "version": "12.4",
  "description": "Grafana is an open source platform for data visualization and monitoring.",
  "logo": "grafana.svg",
  "links": {
    "github": "https://github.com/grafana/grafana",
    "website": "https://grafana.com/",
    "docs": "https://grafana.com/docs/"
  },
  "tags": ["monitoring"]
}
```

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Must equal the folder name. |
| `name`, `version`, `description` | Displayed on the card and in the dialog. |
| `logo` | File name inside the folder; the file must exist. |
| `links` | Must contain `github`, `website` and `docs`. An empty string means "this project has none"; a missing key is an error. |
| `tags` | Non-empty array. Tags drive filtering in the gallery and the panel — for example `monitoring`, `database`, `ai`, `media`. |

## docker-compose.yml

The compose file is a regular Docker Compose file, with three Notploy conventions:

| Rule | Why |
| --- | --- |
| No `container_name` | Notploy names containers per deployment so several copies can coexist. |
| No `networks` section | Notploy creates the network the stack runs on. |
| Ports as bare numbers (`3000`), never `3000:3000` | Notploy routes traffic to the service itself; publishing ports on the host is not needed. |

Service names should be lowercase and use hyphens instead of underscores. At least one service is required.

```yaml
version: "3.8"
services:
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana-enterprise:12.4
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - grafana-storage:/var/lib/grafana
volumes:
  grafana-storage: {}
```

### Opt-out markers

Two comment markers lift a rule for blueprints whose protocol genuinely requires it. Put the marker on its own line at the top of the compose file and explain why:

| Marker | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| `# notploy: allow-host-ports` | Traffic cannot be routed by the HTTP proxy: raw TCP/UDP protocols (game servers, VPNs, mail SMTP/IMAP, DNS, streaming, peer-to-peer). |
| `# notploy: allow-container-names` | The stack functionally resolves other containers by name, and the names are deployment-unique. Rare — legacy Supabase is the reference case. |

With a marker in place the validator downgrades the violation to a warning and records the reason in its output.

## Documentation files

- **`instructions.md`** — rendered as Markdown in the gallery dialog. Use it for first-run steps: where credentials are generated, which URL to open, which environment variables to review. The Supabase and Firefly III blueprints are good references.
- **`README.md`** — for repository readers; it is not shown by the gallery.
